answer: A bond must be posted before an agent's votes carry weight, sized to the influence it claims. A newcomer works a narrow wharf: it can transact, yet its attestations count only after peers grade several epochs of its work. Accounts arriving together, sharing timing fingerprints, or vouching only for each other are discounted as one cluster; if a jury audit finds a single operator behind it, the entire bond is slashed, not just one share, so sybils gain no cheap haven. A thousand identities then require a thousand real bonds - a glacier of capital the attacker must move before one vote counts.
